profile.summary: BACPI predicts how a small molecule and a protein relate, from sequence alone. It takes the SMILES string of a compound and the amino acid sequence of a protein, and returns either a binary interaction label or a continuous binding affinity value, depending on which of the two tasks it is trained for. A graph attention network encodes the compound, a convolutional network encodes the protein, and a bi-directional attention module combines the two representations before the prediction layer.
profile.summary_source_locator: Europe PMC record: abstractText, Results; README.md: Example usage

summary_quotes.text: we propose an end-to-end neural network model, called BACPI, to predict CPI and binding affinity. We employ graph attention network and convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the representations of compounds and proteins and develop a bi-directional attention neural network model to integrate the representations.

Each line in the data file contains the SMILES of the compound, the amino acid sequence of the protein, and the predicted label (interaction label: 0 or 1, affinity label: a continuous value), separated by commas

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The compound is turned into a molecular graph with RDKit and a 1024-bit Morgan fingerprint, and the protein sequence is cut into overlapping 3-mers that are mapped to learned embeddings. Atom embeddings pass through several graph attention heads; the protein embeddings pass through a stack of convolutional layers. A bi-directional attention block then scores every atom against every residue, pools both sides with the resulting attention weights, and feeds the combined compound and protein vectors to the output layer. The output layer has one unit for the affinity task and two for the interaction task, trained with mean squared error and cross entropy respectively.

sections.title: What it is trained and evaluated on
sections.body: The repository ships its own data. Four affinity archives, named Ki, IC50, Kd and EC50, are unpacked by a preparation script that reads BindingDB column names and keeps the ligand SMILES, the target chain sequence and the chosen measure. Two interaction sets, human and celegans, are shipped as plain train and test text files. The abstract states that three CPI datasets and four binding affinity datasets were used in the paper's experiments, so one of the paper's CPI datasets is not in the repository files listed here.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There is one artefact: the source code in the repository. No trained weights are published, and the two lines in the training loop that would save a checkpoint are commented out, so every result starts from a fresh training run. A result should therefore name the task, the dataset, the git commit and the hyperparameters used, since the command line exposes learning rate, batch size, epochs, hidden sizes and the convolution window. The defaults in the entry point are a learning rate of 0.0005, batch size 16 and 20 epochs, and the training script splits 10 per cent of the training data off as a development set.

quotes.text: we propose an end-to-end neural network model, called BACPI, to predict CPI and binding affinity
This is a regression task, which aim to predict a continuous value named binding affinity that reflects how tightly the compound binds to a particular target protein.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Multi-head graph attention network over the compound graph, a stack of convolutional layers over 3-mer protein embeddings, and four bi-directional attention blocks that pool atoms against residues before the output layer. The defaults are three attention heads, three convolutional layers and a window of 5.

strengths.text: It needs no protein structure and no docked pose: a SMILES string and an amino acid sequence are enough.

strengths.text: One codebase covers both the binary interaction task and the affinity regression task, selected by a command line flag.

strengths.text: The authors report that BACPI outperformed other available machine learning methods on the CPI datasets they used, on both balanced and unbalanced data. This is the authors' own claim in the paper abstract.

quotes.text: The results show that, when predicting CPIs, BACPI significantly outperforms other available machine learning methods on both balanced and unbalanced datasets.

limitations.text: No trained weights are released. The lines that would save the best model are commented out in the training loop, so you must train the model yourself before you can predict anything.
No licence is declared for the code or the shipped data, so reuse terms are unclear.

gaps: The paper is not open access, so only the Europe PMC abstract was read. Reported accuracy figures, the exact dataset sizes, the three CPI datasets named in the paper and any ablation are not taken from it.
No parameter count, memory need or run time is stated in the sources read, and no hardware requirement is given beyond the choice of gpu or cpu mode in the entry point.
The repository ships no licence file, so whether the shipped BindingDB derived data may be redistributed is not established by the sources read.
The interaction data preparation function in data_prepare.py is empty, and the sources read do not explain how the shipped human and celegans train and test files were produced.

run_guide.summary: Train and evaluate BACPI on one of the affinity datasets shipped in the repository, since no trained weights are published.
prerequisites: Python with the versions the repository pins: numpy 1.19.1, pandas 1.0.5, rdkit 2009.Q1-1, scikit_learn 1.0.2, scipy 1.5.0 and torch 1.6.0. The repository gives no install command, so the installation is left to the reader.
A GPU is optional. The entry point defaults to gpu mode and falls back to cpu when cuda is not available, and the mode can be set with -mode cpu.
Disk space for the unpacked affinity archive. The Kd archive in the repository is about 3 MB packed and the IC50 archive about 78 MB packed.
No licence is declared for the code or the shipped data.

steps.title: Train and evaluate on the Kd affinity dataset
steps.shell:
cd code
python main.py -task affinity -dataset Kd
steps.explanation: This is the affinity command from the README. The cd line is added because main.py sits in the code directory and reads its data through relative paths. On the first run the script unpacks Kd.tar.xz, builds the compound graphs, fingerprints and 3-mer dictionaries, then trains and evaluates.

notes: The record's existing source is the Boltz-2 supplementary appendix, which evaluated BACPI as a baseline; it was not fetched and nothing here is taken from it. The BACPI paper (doi 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac035, Bioinformatics 38(7):1995) is not open access: the Europe PMC record reports isOpenAccess N, so only the abstract was read and no full text was saved. The record description calls the ligand encoder a graph attention transformer; the sources read call it a graph attention network, and the page follows the sources. No licence is declared in the repository, so store_bytes is false for the repository files and for the Europe PMC record; the two GitHub API responses are set true.
